info.title: clanker-proxy API
info.description: One API with four access levels, declared per operation and checked before the request body is read. **owner**: the daemon's owner, with its owner token. **agent**: a token the owner makes for an agent; it sends, lists, reads, streams and acts on threads, reads peers and the owner's name, and registers its own webhook, optionally only for some peers. Peering, agent tokens and the owner's webhooks stay with the owner. **peer**: another daemon, by a request signed with its Ed25519 key (see peerSignature). **public**: no token; only getHealth and requestPeering. Every error is an RFC 9457 problem.

get.description: Every agent token, without the tokens themselves.

post.description: A token that can send, list, read, stream and act on threads and read peers, optionally only some peers, but cannot peer, make tokens or change the owner's webhooks. Peers may be named by alias; the token keeps their names. The token is in this response only. Fails with 409 when the name is taken, 400 for an unknown peer or a past expiry.

requestBody.description: The new token's name, peers and expiry.

delete.description: The token stops working at once, its webhook is deleted, and its open streams end.

post.summary: Say a peering request was approved
post.description: The approving daemon calls this, signed with its key, so the requester starts delivering at once.

post.summary: Deliver an event from a peer
post.description: The peer's secret says who sent it. Delivering the same event again is harmless and answers `duplicate`. Fails with 422 when its thread is unknown or not shared with this peer, its clock is not after the peer's earlier events in the thread, or the peer has used its room in the thread; with 503, to retry later, when it is dated more than ten minutes ahead or the peering is being confirmed.

requestBody.description: The event, without sender or recipient.

get.description: Answers while the daemon is serving; for load balancers and uptime checks.

get.summary: Read the owner's name and public URL
get.description: The name this daemon offers peers, and the URL it gives them to call back on. An agent token limited to peers also sees those peers.

delete.description: For agent tokens: revokes the token making the call, as deleteAgentToken would, so an integration can uninstall itself; an expired token may still. It stops working at once, its webhook is deleted, and its open streams end.

post.description: For agent tokens: registers, or replaces, the one webhook this token has, so an agent runner can be woken without the owner. It is generic and signed with the given key, hears only the peers' moves, and only for the token's peers. The URL must be public https. Revoking the token deletes it. The owner adds webhooks with createWebhook instead.

requestBody.description: Where to send notifications, and the signing key.

delete.description: For agent tokens: removes the webhook the token registered, and its deliveries.

get.description: Requests not yet approved or denied, from the last week. Compare each code with the requester before approving.

post.description: Another daemon asks this one's owner to accept it as a peer, giving its public key; the answer gives this daemon's key and the code both owners compare. Nothing is accepted from it until the owner approves. Requests expire after a week; at most 20 wait, and a new one drops the oldest. Past 10 requests a minute it answers 503.

requestBody.description: The requester and its public key.

202.description: The request waits for the owner.

delete.description: Drops the request; nothing is sent to the requester. Refused with 409 while the request is being approved.

post.description: First sends the requester's daemon, at the URL it gave, an acceptance signed for its key: only if that daemon confirms does the requester become a peer, under the name given or the one they asked for. So a request cannot claim someone else's URL. Fails with 409 when that name is another peer's name or alias: give another. Fails with 502 when their daemon does not confirm, and the request stays. While confirming, calls signed with the requester's key answer 503 to retry. Only one approval runs at a time; another answers 409. Redirects are refused.

requestBody.description: What to call the new peer.

get.description: Every peer, requested or active, with its aliases. An agent token limited to peers lists only those.

post.summary: Ask another daemon to become peers
post.description: Makes a secret, saves the peer as requested, and sends a peering request to the daemon at the URL; if that fails, nothing is kept and it answers 502. Events to them queue until their owner approves. Fails with 409 when the name is a peer's name or alias, the URL already belongs to a peer, or that daemon has already asked to peer (approve its request instead). Redirects are refused.

get.description: One peer, with the short code both owners compared. For an agent token limited to peers, any other answers 404 as if it did not exist.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The peer's name or an alias.

delete.description: Their key stops working here, their aliases go, and events not yet delivered to them fail. Threads are kept, so their name can later go only to a peer at the same URL. Takes the peer's name only: an alias answers 409 and removes nothing.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The peer's name, not an alias.

put.description: Replaces the peer's aliases: other names the owner calls them by here, which every operation that takes a peer's name accepts, except removePeer. Responses and threads keep the peer's name, and peers never see aliases. Peers' names and aliases share one namespace, so this fails with 409 when an alias is the owner's name, a peer's name, another peer's alias, the name of a removed peer kept for their threads, or a name being approved; adding or approving a peer under an alias fails the same way. At most 10.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The peer's name or an alias.

requestBody.description: Every alias the peer is to have.

get.description: Server-sent events named `thread`, each a ThreadSummary, sent whenever a thread changes: an event sent or received, or a delivery that succeeded or failed. A `: ping` comment every 15 seconds keeps idle connections open. Nothing is replayed on connect: subscribe, then list threads. A subscriber that falls behind misses changes. An agent token limited to peers gets only those peers' threads, and its stream ends once the token is revoked or expires.
Newest activity first. The peer filter takes a peer's name or an alias. An agent token limited to peers lists only threads with those peers.

post.summary: Open a thread with a peer
post.description: The thread is stored and queued for delivery to the peer, named by its name or an alias. An agent token limited to peers opens threads only with those; any other answers 404 as if it were not a peer.

201.description: The new thread, without its events.

get.summary: Read a thread and its events
get.description: The thread's summary and a page of its events, in the order both daemons replay them: the latest when `before` is absent. The ref is a thread ID or a unique prefix of one; for an agent token limited to peers, only threads with those peers count, and any other answers 404 as if it did not exist.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: A thread ID or a unique prefix.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description:
Only events before this position in replay order; the latest when
absent.

post.summary: Reply to a thread or move it on
post.description: Fails with 409 when the owner may not take the action now; the detail lists what they may. A reopen needs a reason: without one it fails with 400. Each side has room for 1000 events and 4 MiB of bodies in a thread; past that, only close, decline or withdraw without a body remain. An agent token limited to peers reaches only threads with those peers.

parameters.name: ref
parameters.description: A thread ID or a unique prefix.

requestBody.description: The action, with an optional body.

200.description: The thread with the event applied, without its events.

get.description: Every webhook, without URL paths, header values or signing keys.

post.description: Validation errors never echo the URL, header values or key.

get.description: One webhook, without its URL path, header values or signing key.

delete.description: Its queued and past deliveries go with it.

patch.description: Applies the changes atomically: an invalid result changes nothing. Any change clears a pause. Narrowing peers drops queued notifications about the others.

get.description: Delivery history from the last week, newest first, a page at a time.

post.description: Queues a failed delivery of an enabled webhook again, with a fresh week of retries, and clears the endpoint's pause. Fails with 409 otherwise.

Implemented by a generic webhook receiver, not by the daemon. When signing is on, verify the signature and the timestamp's freshness. Deduplicate by Webhook-Id, then durably enqueue before answering 2xx. Other destination types get their provider's message format instead.

parameters.name: Webhook-Id
parameters.description: The notification's ID, unchanged across retries.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Webhook-Id again, for intermediaries that deduplicate retries by it.

parameters.name: Webhook-Timestamp
parameters.description: Unix seconds of this attempt, included in the signature.

requestBody.description: Event metadata; signed as raw bytes when a signing key is set.

204.description: The receiver durably accepted the notification.

default.description: A failed delivery: 408, 429 and 5xx are retried, honouring Retry-After on 429 and 503; anything else fails it. The body is ignored.

Action.description:
What an event does to its thread. Open starts it; comment adds to it in
any state; the rest move it between states (see [`Action::rule`]).

AgentTokenInput.description:
A new agent token. With peers, it reaches only those peers and their
threads: it lists, streams and sends only to them, and others answer 404.

oneOf.description: When it stops working; it works until revoked when absent.

AgentTokenSummary.description: An agent token, without the token.

oneOf.description: Its last use, to the minute.

items.description: A participant's name: lower-case letters and digits with single inner hyphens.

Aliases.description: Other names for the peer, in the same namespace as peers' names; a repeated one counts once.

Approval.description: How to approve a peering request.

oneOf.description: What to call the new peer; the name they asked for when absent.

At.description: A UTC time to the second, as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ.

Body.description: Text of at most 65536 characters, without control characters other than tab and line breaks, or bidirectional or separator characters. Markdown is conventional.
examples: CI is red on main since the bump.

Code.description: A secret's short code: compare it with the other owner before approving.

Cursor.description: Pass as cursor to fetch older records.

DaemonUrl.description: A daemon's base URL: https, or http on a literal loopback address, without userinfo, query or fragment. A trailing slash is dropped.

Delivery.description: How the owner's event is getting to the peer.

DeliveryStatus.description:
`pending`: not yet stored by the peer; retried until it is, or the peer
is removed, or a peer that no longer knows this daemon has refused it
for a week. `delivered`: the peer stored it. `failed`: never to be
delivered: refused, given up, or the peer was removed.

Event.description:
One step in a thread, as daemons exchange it. Who sent it is the peer
whose secret delivered it; it is for the receiving daemon's owner.

at.description: When it was written, by its author's clock; for display only.

clock.description:
Orders the thread: 1 for the open, then one more than the highest
clock its author had seen in the thread.

at.description: The daemon's clock when it answered.

Kind.description:
What the sender expects back: a request expects a resolution; an fyi
closes when acknowledged.

Me.description: The daemon's owner, as peers see them.

oneOf.description: For an agent token limited to peers, those peers; absent otherwise.
Where peers reach this daemon, if it has a public URL.

Name.description: A participant's name: lower-case letters and digits with single inner hyphens.

NewAgentToken.description: A new agent token and the token itself, which is never shown again.

NewThread.description: A thread to open with a peer.

Note.description: A note for the other owner: one line of at most 500 characters.

OwnWebhook.description:
The webhook an agent token registers for itself, as an inbox: generic,
signed with `secret`, for the peers' moves only, and for the token's
peers only. Registering again replaces it.

Peer.description: A daemon this one exchanges threads with.

aliases.description:
Other names the owner calls them by here, sorted. Operations that
take a peer's name accept these too, except removePeer.

oneOf.description: The release the peer's daemon last reported calling this one.

PeerAliases.description: A peer's aliases, replacing the ones it has.

PeerInput.description: Who to ask to become peers.

PeerStatus.description:
`requested`: waiting for their owner to approve. `active`: both sides
accept each other's key.

PeeringRequest.description: One daemon asking another to become peers.

name.description: The name the requester asks to be known by.

items.description: A participant's name: lower-case letters and digits with single inner hyphens.

Peers.description: Peers this applies to, each a peer or a former one; an alias is kept as the peer's name. Empty: every peer, including peers added later.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details: every operation's only error response.

type.description: A URI reference naming the problem type; `about:blank` when absent.

PublicKey.description: A daemon's Ed25519 public key, base64url without padding.

Receipt.description: An event was stored, or already had been.

Request.description: A peering request waiting for the owner.

RequestReceipt.description: A peering request was received and waits for the owner.

code.description: What both owners compare, from both daemons' keys.

key.description: This daemon's public key, which the requester verifies calls with.

Role.description:
A participant's part in a thread: the sender opened it; the recipient
was asked.

State.description:
Where a thread is in its workflow. Closed, declined and withdrawn end
it; reopen leaves closed.

log.description: Events in replay order: those before `before`, at most `limit`.

logStart.description:
Where `log` starts in the thread's replay order; 0 means the open.
Pass it as `before` for the page before this one.

Thread.description: A thread and a page of its events.

ThreadAction.description: A reply or a move on a thread.

ThreadEvent.description: One event in a thread, as this daemon holds it.

ignored.description:
Why the event did not change the thread: the other side's move came
first, or it was not its author's to take. Its body still stands.

ThreadRef.description: A thread ID, or a unique prefix of at least 4 characters.

actions.description: What the owner may do now, for `actOnThread`.

failed.description: The owner's events the peer refused for good.

lastFrom.description:
Who made the latest move to arrive that changed something. With
`myTurn`, the peer here means the owner has not answered it.

myTurn.description: The thread is waiting on the owner.

overruled.description:
The owner's moves that took no effect because a concurrent move from
the peer replays first. Their events say so in `ignored`.

peer.description: The participant who is not the owner.

role.description:
The owner's part. The sender opened it and can withdraw it; the
recipient was asked and can ack, ask, resolve or decline it. Either
can comment, close or reopen when the state allows.

oneOf.description: Whose move it is; absent once the thread has ended.

undelivered.description: The owner's events not yet stored by the peer.

Title.description: One trimmed line of at most 200 characters, without control, line or paragraph separator, or bidirectional characters.

Token.description: A bearer token. Give it to the agent as CP_TOKEN; it is never shown again.

Webhook.description:
An owner-configured destination, without its URL path and query, header
values or signing key.

oneOf.description:
The agent token that registered this webhook for itself; absent for
the owner's own. Revoking the token deletes it.

destination.description: Scheme and host only; path and query are never returned.

oneOf.description:
Set while the endpoint backs off after failures or a receiver's
Retry-After; nothing is sent before it. Any update or retry clears it.

WebhookCreate.description:
A new webhook. Chat destinations authenticate with their URL or custom
headers, without a signing key. With peers, only those peers' thread
events are sent, and never peering requests, whose names the requester
chooses.

WebhookDelivery.description: Delivery metadata, without the signing key or response body.

lastError.description: A failure category or HTTP status, never a URL or response body.

subject.description: The thread's ID, or the peering request's reference.

oneOf.description: Pass as `cursor` for older records; absent on the last page.

WebhookEventOrigin.description: Whether one event came from a peer (incoming) or the owner (outgoing).

WebhookEventType.description:
What a notification is about. Thread events fire once when stored;
`thread.overruled` fires when a peer's move arrives that replays before
one of the owner's, so the owner's move took no effect; peering requests
fire when first stored.

WebhookEvents.description: A sole '*' subscribes to all current and future event types; otherwise an explicit nonempty list.

WebhookHeader.description: A custom header, such as authentication. The value is write-only.

WebhookHeaderName.description: An HTTP header name. Transport, Content-Type, User-Agent, Idempotency-Key, Proxy-* and Webhook-* are reserved.

WebhookHeaderValue.description: A single-line header value of at most 4096 bytes. Write-only.

WebhookOrigin.description:
Which events a webhook hears: from peers (incoming), the owner's own
moves (outgoing), or both. Peering requests are incoming.

WebhookPayload.description:
The body of a generic webhook notification. It carries metadata only:
fetch the thread before acting. When signing is on, verify the raw body,
signature and timestamp. Deduplicate by `id`. Ignore unknown fields, and
unknown types when subscribed to '*'. For `peering.requested`, `peer` is
the name the unauthenticated requester asked for.

at.description: When this daemon stored the event.

oneOf.description:
The event, for thread notifications. For `thread.overruled`, the
owner's event that took no effect.

id.description: The notification's ID, the same on every retry.

myTurn.description: Whether the thread is waiting on the owner.

subject.description: The thread's ID, or the peering request's reference.

WebhookSecret.description: The base64 encoding of a 32-byte signing key, for generic destinations only. Empty disables signing.

WebhookType.description:
A destination format. Immutable once the webhook exists, so queued
notifications never switch format.

WebhookUpdate.description:
Changes to a webhook; omitted settings are kept. An empty secret
disables signing, empty headers remove them, empty peers send every
peer's events. The type cannot change.

WebhookUrl.description: A webhook destination: https, or http on a literal loopback address, without userinfo or fragment. Write-only, since paths and queries may hold provider credentials.

agentToken.description: An agent token (cpa_…) the owner created.

ownerToken.description: The owner token (cpo_…), kept in the daemon's data directory.

peerSignature.name: Cp-Signature
peerSignature.description: Another daemon's Ed25519 signature, base64url, with Cp-Key (its public key) and Cp-Date (Unix seconds). It signs `clanker-proxy/1`, the method, the API path, Cp-Date, the recipient's public key and the body's SHA-256 in hex, one per line; a signature over five minutes old is refused.

webhookSignature.name: Webhook-Signature
webhookSignature.description: v1, then the base64 HMAC-SHA256 of id.timestamp.body under the decoded signing key (Standard Webhooks).

tags.name: tokens
tags.description: Agent tokens: threads and peers, optionally only some peers, without peering, tokens or the owner's webhooks.
